questions.question: What license should this project carry?

options.label: MIT
options.description: Permissive, shortest, most common for tooling of this kind. Anyone may use, modify and redistribute, including commercially, with attribution. Cost: no protection against someone repackaging it closed-source.

options.label: Apache 2.0
options.description: Permissive like MIT, plus an explicit patent grant and a requirement to state changes. Cost: longer text, slightly more ceremony for contributors.

options.label: Leave it unlicensed for now
options.description: Change nothing. Cost: with no license stated, others technically have no right to use or redistribute it at all — which is the opposite of what publishing it implies, and the ambiguity sits on every existing install.

questions.question: Should the development-rules file keep shipping to people who install this?

options.label: Accept it, and write down why (Recommended)
options.description: Leave the packaging alone and record the decision plus the warning, so it reads as chosen rather than unnoticed. Cost: strangers still receive instructions that mean nothing to them, and the load warning keeps printing.

options.label: Exclude it from the package
options.description: Add a packaging step so development-only files stay out of installs. Cost: a new mechanism to maintain, and anything mis-listed goes missing from installs silently — a worse failure than the current noise.

questions.question: Add the missing worked examples to the five background helpers?

options.label: Not now — file it as its own card (Recommended)
options.description: Record it as separate work. Cost: the helpers stay harder to pick correctly until someone does it.

options.label: Do it now
options.description: Write examples for all five in this session. Cost: substantial writing across five files unrelated to the current feature, and a badly-chosen example actively mis-trains selection — worse than none.

options.label: Do just the two used most
options.description: Examples for the two that get invoked most often, card for the rest. Cost: a partly-done convention is the kind of thing that never gets finished.
